hints: Focus on counting carbon atoms carefully, the product acid must have the same number of carbons as the starting organic molecule.
Notice that statement 1 starts from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ which has three carbons in total, so think about how many carbons its acid product must have.

Recall that primary alcohols and aldehydes oxidise without losing carbon, while nitrile hydrolysis also keeps the nitrile carbon as the $\text{COOH}$ carbon, then check which two statements keep the carbon count.
walkthrough:
**Check Statement 1 - Nitrile Hydrolysis**

Hydrolysis of a nitrile with aqueous acid gives a carboxylic acid with the same number of carbons. The $\text{CN}$ carbon becomes the $\text{COOH}$ carbon.

$$\text{R-CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Apply Carbon Counting to Statement 1**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ has 3 carbons, so it must give propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, not ethanoic acid which has only 2 carbons. So statement 1 is incorrect.

**Check Statements 2 and 3 - Oxidation**

Strong oxidation of a primary alcohol gives the carboxylic acid with the same carbon skeleton. So $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (4 carbons) gives butanoic acid (4 carbons).

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Confirm Aldehyde Oxidation**

Oxidation of an aldehyde also keeps all carbons. So $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ (3 carbons) gives propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (3 carbons).

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

Therefore only statements 2 and 3 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is wrong as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ gives propanoic acid, not ethanoic acid. Students choosing this forget to count the nitrile carbon.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes statement 1. Statement 1 confuses ethanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$ gives ethanoic acid) with propanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ gives propanoic acid).
options.C: Correct because only 2 and 3 are true. Butan-1-ol oxidises to butanoic acid and propanal oxidises to propanoic acid, both with no change in carbon number. Statement 1 is false due to wrong carbon count.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes statement 1 with statement 3. Statement 1 is the trap, hydrolysis retains the $\text{CN}$ carbon so the product has one more carbon than claimed.
